_rules: AUTHORING RULES FOR FUTURE BUILDERS. Read docs/ORIGIN.md and docs/STYLE.md first.
1. One document per place kind. The key in `fragments` is the kind id (src/world/kinds/<id>.js). Every kind must have one; the game places it on a stand just inside the place's first door.

2. Each document reveals ONE thread from ORIGIN.md (name it in `thread`), from inside the world: a brochure, memo, chart, card, letter, log. Never narrate the backstory, never explain what is happening, never confirm a theory. The player should finish reading with a better question, not an answer.

3. Voice and era: 1971-1979, a research institute pretending to be a motor hotel. Typewriter or careful handwriting. Plain, specific details (room numbers, dollar amounts, form numbers) beat adjectives.
4. Never write a clock time that moves. Watches have no hands. Use '--:--' or leave times blank. The tape stamp (3:14 AM, MAR. 14 1979) belongs to the camera, not to documents.
5. Banned: gore, bodies, blood, the words monster / dimension / backrooms / portal / loop, jokes that wink at the player, modern words. Nothing in a document may contradict ORIGIN.md.
6. Length: `body` at most ~120 words. `[[text]]` renders as a redaction bar (use at most two per document). `\n` is a line break.
7. `log` is the logbook line the player writes after reading: first person, past tense, at most 25 words, states what was read, not what it means.
8. `head` is the document's own header line (form title, letterhead, label). `sign` is an optional signature or footer.

9. Threads in use so far: volunteers, watches, checkingOut, keepLightsOn, halesPlans, theSeal. Spread new documents across threads; do not reveal theSeal or the end of halesPlans in a place that is common.

lobby.head: ASTER-VALE FOUNDATION  -  A RESTFUL WEEK AT THE MERIDIAN LODGE
lobby.body:
Tired of being tired?

The Aster-Vale Foundation invites healthy adults, 21 to 55, to spend seven restful days at the Meridian Lodge as paid guests of our Continuous Habitation program.

  - $40.00 per day, paid at check-out
  - Private room, color television, meals at all hours
  - Every room lit for your comfort, day and night

There are no chores and no schedules. You will not be asked to do anything at all, except stay.

Please leave your wristwatch at the Front Desk on arrival. A Lodge watch will be issued.
lobby.sign: Form AV-7 (rev. 1973). Detach and return the card below to reserve your week.
lobby.log: A brochure at the front desk: paid volunteers, a restful week, every room lit day and night. Leave your watch at the desk.

guestRooms.head: POSTCARD  -  THE MERIDIAN LODGE (not mailed)
guestRooms.body:
Ruth -

Day four, I think. Or five. They took my watch at the desk like the paper said and gave me a Lodge watch. It has no hands. I laughed. The clerk didn't.

I feel fine. That's the thing. I haven't been tired since the first night and I don't miss it. The lamp is always on and the TV is always on and somebody is always walking past the door.

I asked a maid what time it was. She said it's the same time it's been.

Forty dollars a day. Tell the boys I'll be home when the week's up.
guestRooms.log: An unmailed postcard from a guest named Walt. They took his watch and gave him one with no hands. He felt fine.

iceVending.head: MEMORANDUM  -  TO: ALL STAFF  -  FROM: DR. I. VARGA  -  RE: FIXTURES
iceVending.body:
Effective immediately:

1. No fixture in the Lodge is to be allowed to go dark. Not for cleaning, not for repair, not for a guest's comfort.

2. A failing tube is to be reported at once and replaced within the hour. Carry spares.

3. If a room cannot be relit, vacate it, shut the door and report the room number to the Front Desk. Do not re-enter it to check. It will not be the same room.

4. The night shift will walk every hall continuously.

The building does what we teach it. We are teaching it [[to stay awake]].
iceVending.sign: Posted by the ice machine, Copy 3 of 12
iceVending.log: A memo from Dr. Varga, taped by the ice machine: no light may ever go dark. A dark room is to be shut and never re-entered.

ballroom.head: THE STARLIGHT BALLROOM  -  WELCOME DINNER FOR OUR NEW GUESTS
ballroom.body:
Tonight's Programme

  Dinner is served ..... --:--

laundry.head: SOUTHERN VALLEY POWER CO.  -  SERVICE DISCONNECT ORDER  -  W.O. 79-0314
laundry.body:
Premises: Meridian Lodge, ridge road (no number)
Requested by: Aster-Vale Fdn., legal dept.

1. Main panel located, laundry level. All 40 breakers thrown to OFF.  -- done
2. Service drop cut at pole.  -- done
3. Meter sealed and tagged.  -- done
4. Verify zero load.

Remarks: meter disc still turning. Read 3 times. Load steady, same as before disconnect. Lights in building remain on. Could not find what they are wired to.

Crew would not go back inside to check. [[             ]]. Recommend this be left as is.
laundry.sign: Lineman: R. Okafor. Foreman's signature: (not signed)
laundry.log: A disconnect order from the power company. Every breaker was thrown and the line was cut. The meter kept turning and the lights stayed on.

draftingOffice.head: INTEROFFICE  -  TO: DR. I. VARGA  -  FROM: D. HALE, NIGHT ARCHITECT
draftingOffice.body:
Ilse,

You asked for a current plan. I can't give you one. I measure a hall, come back to the board, and the hall I measured has already changed to match the drawing. So I drew a short one. In the morning it was short.

I have stopped drawing doors. I have stopped drawing anything I would not want to walk into.

I am no longer sure I am drawing what is there. I am beginning to think it is [[waiting to see what I draw]].

Please do not ask me for room 240 again. I never drew it.
draftingOffice.log: A memo from Desmond Hale to Dr. Varga. He measured halls that changed to match his drawings, and stopped drawing doors.
